Hey Elizabeth! thanks so much for the kind words, and I really appreciate you being upfront about budget. That makes it a lot easier to find the right fit.

I actually work on flat project rates rather than hourly, which most clients find more straightforward — you know exactly what you're getting and what it costs before we start, with no surprises.

For a resume and cover letter, my standard package starts at $150. That includes a thorough intake process where I learn about your background and goals, a fully ATS-optimized resume in Word and PDF, a tailored cover letter, and a round of revisions to make sure everything feels right.

Turnaround is typically 2-3 business days from the time I have everything I need from you.

If budget is a constraint right now, I'm happy to talk through options — sometimes it makes sense to start with the resume alone and add the cover letter once you're ready. Either way, I want to make sure you end up with something that actually works for you.

What does your timeline look like, and do you have a sense of the types of roles you're targeting?

So standard will be, as far as deliverables, a fully ATS-optimized resume in Word and PDF, a tailored cover letter, and a round of revisions.
With how things are in the hiring market nowadays, I've begun making a lot of clients a "Standard" version and a "Signature" version of their resume.
**Standard Edition**
This is the clean, professional version built for function. It's fully ATS-optimized, meaning it's formatted to pass through the automated screening systems most companies use before a human ever sees it. You get a Word and PDF version you can easily update yourself. This is the right choice if you're applying online and want something polished and recruiter-ready.

**Signature Edition**
This is everything in the Standard, plus a visually designed version — built in Canva — that's branded to you. It's eye-catching, modern, and great for sending directly to a hiring manager, sharing at networking events, or posting to your portfolio. It stands out in a way a traditional resume simply can't. This is the tier most of my clients go with when presentation matters as much as content.

**Cover Letter**
A fully tailored letter written in your voice, aligned to your target role. Not a generic template — an actual narrative that complements your resume and gives you something compelling to say. Which I do the same as with resumes a standard one and a signature one aligned with the design style created for your signature edition resume.

A lot of clients also get a LinkedIn Optimization as part of the package. This goes well beyond copying your resume onto your profile. I rewrite your headline, About section, and experience entries to work with LinkedIn's search algorithm so recruiters can actually find you. I also advise on keywords, profile settings, and how to position yourself for the roles you're targeting.

What's your situation — are you actively applying now, or more in the early stages of figuring out your next move? Do you have an idea on your budget?

The short answer: the content is the same. Both versions go through the same writing process — the same research, strategy, and carefully crafted bullets. The difference is purely in presentation.

The Standard is a clean, professionally formatted Word/PDF document. It's built to perform — ATS-friendly, easy to read, and completely functional for any application.

The Signature takes that same content and gives it a designed look — custom layout, typography, and visual branding built in Canva. It's the version that makes someone stop scrolling when it lands in their inbox. A lot of clients use both: the Standard for online applications where ATS is a factor, and the Signature for direct outreach or networking situations where standing out visually matters.

It was great connecting with you! As promised, I’ve attached your intake questionnaire — this is how I gather everything I need to put together a strong first draft on my end.

I know it looks like a lot, but don’t feel pressured to have every answer perfectly worded. Notes, bullet points, and rough thoughts are completely fine. The more detail you can give me, the better I can tell your story — but even partial answers give me a solid starting point to work from.

A few sections worth paying extra attention to:
∙	The current role section — since you wear a lot of hats, I want to make sure nothing gets left out
∙	The side work section — that experience is more valuable than most people realize, and I want to position it in a way that works in your favor
∙	The job target section — even a general direction helps me tailor the language and focus of the document

Once I receive the completed questionnaire, I’ll be in touch with a timeline for your first draft.
Feel free to reach out if any of the questions are unclear or if you’d like to talk through anything before filling it out.

Hi Elizabeth,

First drafts are ready for your review! I've attached your Standard and Signature editions of both the resume and cover letter, so four documents total.

Quick orientation on what you're looking at:

The **Standard editions** are your ATS-optimized Word and PDF versions, built to pass through automated screening systems for online applications. Clean, professional, easy for you to update yourself down the road.

The **Signature editions** are the designed Canva versions, branded to you and built to stand out when you're sending directly to a hiring manager, networking, or following up after a conversation. Same content, different presentation.

A few things to know as you read through:

Since your questionnaire had some open spots, I filled in a few gaps with educated guesses based on your old resume. The big ones are your timeline (San Jose Options as 2010 to 2021, your independent personal assistant work as 2011 to 2021, and Teamraderie from April 2021 forward), and the positioning, which I aimed at Executive/Personal Assistant roles since that's where your experience is strongest. I also cut Macy's since it's older than 20 years and didn't add to the story.

I've attached a short follow-up document with a handful of quick questions, mostly to confirm dates and pull out a few specific wins from your Teamraderie role. Even a few words on each will let me sharpen the next draft considerably.

Take your time reading through everything. When you're ready, send back any edits, reactions, or answers to those questions and I'll fold them in. The first round of revisions is included, so don't hold back, this is the time to tell me what feels right and what doesn't.

Looking forward to your thoughts!

Colin

Hi Elizabeth,

I'm so sorry, I had reviewed the answers but then at some point had it in my mind I was waiting for a response for you, my bad! But they were really helpful, and I've gone through and updated both the resume and cover letter to reflect everything you shared. New versions are attached.

A few things to know about what changed:

The biggest shift is the overall positioning. Based on what you said about being open to something new and not necessarily targeting assistant roles, I rebuilt the resume around remote operations instead. The headline, summary, and core competencies now lead with operations, logistics, customer relations, and process building, which opens you up to a much wider set of remote roles (operations coordinator, customer operations, logistics coordinator, project coordinator, that kind of range) without losing the personal assistant experience, which is still in your work history. The cover letter follows the same direction and explicitly names the kinds of roles you are open to, so a hiring manager is not left guessing.

I also corrected the timeline: San Jose Options now shows 2010 to 2014, and your independent personal assistant work shows 2011 to Present with a small "(Concurrent)" note so the overlap with Teamraderie reads as intentional rather than confusing. Let me know if you would rather drop that label, totally optional.

Your FIDM credential is now properly listed (Associate of Arts in Merchandise Marketing), and I leaned into your "built everything from the ground up" answer for Teamraderie. That actually became one of the strongest parts of the resume, your builder mindset comes through really clearly.

If anything reads off, dates that need adjusting, language that does not sound like you, anything missing, just let me know and I will fold it in.

Take your time, no rush.

Thank you,
Colin
